name: Home Assistant
description: Let agents read your home's state and, with approval, control devices through Home Assistant's Assist API.

methods.whenToUse: Recommended. Use a long-lived access token from a dedicated non-admin Home Assistant user, reached over HTTPS (Home Assistant Cloud remote URL or your own TLS reverse proxy).
methods.guidanceMd: Connect to the Model Context Protocol Server integration on your own Home Assistant (2026.8 or newer) over HTTPS. Create a long-lived access token while signed in as a dedicated non-admin Home Assistant user, then paste it below.
methods.label: Use a long-lived access token

tenantFields.label: Home Assistant host
tenantFields.helperMd: Enter the HTTPS host name of your Home Assistant without https:// or a path, for example your Home Assistant Cloud remote URL host or your reverse proxy's host.

tenantFields.label: HTTPS port
tenantFields.helperMd: Use 443 for Home Assistant Cloud and most reverse proxies. Use 8123 only when Home Assistant itself serves HTTPS.

credentialFields.label: Long-lived access token
credentialFields.placeholder: Paste the token from Profile, Security, Long-lived access tokens
credentialFields.helperMd: Long-lived access tokens are not scoped: the token acts as its Home Assistant user. Create it under Profile, Security as a dedicated non-admin user, and expose only needed entities to Assist.

warnings: Long-lived access tokens are not scoped. The token can do anything its Home Assistant user can, so create it as a dedicated non-admin user and never use an owner or administrator token.
Home Assistant has no read-only Assist mode. Agents can only reach entities exposed to Assist, so expose only what agents need under Settings, Voice assistants, Expose.
Device control, scripts, timers, and other non-read tools start as Ask first, and tools that appear later stay quarantined until reviewed.
Home Assistant reached over plain HTTP on a local network cannot use this connector. Use Home Assistant Cloud or an HTTPS reverse proxy.

setupPrerequisite.title: Prepare Home Assistant before connecting
setupPrerequisite.description: Paperclip connects to the official Model Context Protocol Server integration on your own Home Assistant. It must be reachable over HTTPS and run Home Assistant 2026.8 or newer.
steps: In Home Assistant, open Settings, Devices & services, Add integration, and add Model Context Protocol Server with the Assist API selected.
Create a dedicated non-admin Home Assistant user for Paperclip, sign in as that user, and create a long-lived access token under Profile, Security.
Under Settings, Voice assistants, Expose, expose only the entities agents should read or control.
Make Home Assistant reachable over HTTPS, for example with Home Assistant Cloud remote access or your own TLS reverse proxy.
setupPrerequisite.actionLabel: Open Home Assistant MCP Server docs
